keep: The idea is named in one line up front: a new vector, size |a||b| sin θ, square to both, giving the moment and the motor force. [^1] sits on the size rule.

The picture is the brief's spanner and bolt in 3-D with a view you turn: r, F, the shaded parallelogram whose area is the moment, the moment arrow along the bolt flipping when r and F swap, then the wire between poles with the force square to current and field and zero when they line up.
Worked examples computed from the rule: 150 N at 0.3 m gives 45 N m square on and 22.5 N m at 30°; 10 A in 0.2 m across 0.8 T gives 1.6 N; the practice spanner gives 77.94 N m.

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), ending with two mixed puzzles (11, 12). Each brief misconception has a puzzle with its own wrong pick: cos for sin (4, 10), the direction left out (11), the dot product taken for the cross product (11, 12), the order swapped (8, 12), the right-hand rule in an awkward view (8, turned back after).

The conduit-thread analogy reproduces the main result (the arrow is the way a right-hand thread travels, and flips with the turn) and breaks honestly (a seized bolt still has a moment; travel is set by pitch, not push).
fix: Causal step skipped: why only the square part of F turns the bolt. Say the part along the handle points straight at the bolt, so it has no distance from the bolt to turn about.

Causal step skipped: why the arrow points out of the nut to undo it. Say undoing turns anticlockwise seen from your side, and right fingers curled anticlockwise put the thumb toward you. Also say r and F lie in the plane the spanner turns in, so an arrow square to both lies along the bolt.
Misconception not shown failing with numbers: cos at 30° gives 45 × 0.87 = 38.97 N m, more than the honest 22.5. Show it, and say why it is the part that turns nothing.
The direction-left-out slip is only stated. Tie it to the picture: 45 N m alone does not say undo or do up.
Fleming's left-hand rule is not linked, as the brief asks. Add a rule-of-thumb line that it gives the motor force the same direction as the right-hand curl from current to field.
'A spanner's moment and the force on a motor's wire are both cross products' is loose for the force, which is I times l × B. Say both come from cross products.

faults.causalStepSkipped: two places (why only the square part turns, why undo points out), fixed above
faults.falseAbsolutes: none: 'nothing turns' along the handle and 'no force' along the field hold in the ideal model at those settings; 'square on gives the most' holds for every angle since sin θ is at most 1; the page-turning tip holds whenever the second arrow is less than half a turn anticlockwise from the first, which 'leans up the page' sets up
